newsitem.title: INDIA: Non-aligned ask for special UN meeting on Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Non-aligned ask for special UN meeting on Mideast.

text.p: The Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) on Tuesday called for an emergency session of the U.N. General Assembly to demand that Israel stop a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem and all other settlement activities.

The 113-member organisation said in a special statement that U.N. member states should impose an economic boycott on Israeli companies or agencies operating in "occupied Palestinian territories" and whose activities violate U.N. resolutions.

The statement said "the General Assembly should convene in an emergency special session" to demand the immediate cessation of a Jewish settlement on Jabal Abu Ghneim, a hill in Arab East Jerusalem, and "all other Israeli settlement activities".
Middle East peace talks were halted after Israel began work last month on the settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, also called Har Homa, sparking daily clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops.

NAM said U.N. member states "should prevent assistance being provided by their governmental agencies and nationals to, and the conduct of trade and financial dealings with, Israeli commercial, private or public establishments involved in activities in the occupied Palestinian territory, including Jerusalem" that are contrary to Security Council resolutions.

The Non-Aligned Movement adopted the resolution a day after Palestinian President Yasser Arafat addressed the organisation's two-day meeting of foreign ministers. Arafat accused Israel of declaring war on the Middle East peace process.
Arafat had appealed to the movement to support the Palestinians and urged members to follow recent resolutions of the Arab League seeking to review diplomatic ties with Israel.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu left Washington to return to Israel late on Monday after a tough two-hour meeting with President Bill Clinton failed to revive the Israeli-Palestinian peace talks.
In talks between the two leaders, described as frank and candid, Clinton rebuffed Netanyahu's call for a U.S.-led Middle East summit while trying to revive stalled peace efforts.
